conflicts_found: Goleman's 'EI is twice as important as IQ' claim (from his own consulting firm's internal competency-model analysis) is substantially overstated compared to independent peer-reviewed meta-analytic evidence (Joseph & Newman, 2010), which finds ability-based EI adds negligible predictive power once personality and cognitive ability are controlled for.

Self-report ('mixed') EI measures correlate much more strongly with outcomes than performance-based ability EI tests, suggesting self-report EI surveys may partly reflect self-rating bias rather than pure skill.

Whether the ability model has three or four branches is not fully settled among researchers; the four-branch version is presented as the current standard framework without claiming total scientific unanimity.
